subject: Post-call follow-up: candidate models, JSON-schema QA & fn-call retry plan
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Hart <alex.hart@novacare.com>, Priya Sethi <priya.sethi@novacare.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call follow-up: candidate models, JSON-schema QA & fn-call retry plan

Hi Alex / Priya — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps focused on the evaluation pieces we discussed (model fit, structured output conformance, and fn-call retry behavior). I put concrete artifacts/links at the bottom.

Highlights from the call:
- Primary goal: replace NovaCare's current rule-based intake parsing with a model-driven structured extraction flow (JSON schema output) and use tool-calls for downstream validation + enrichment.
- Constraints: average payload size ~1.2k chars, 95th percentile latency goal <= 350ms, and strict schema compliance for downstream ETL.
- Success metric: schema-validation pass rate >= 98% on the 2,000-sample test set and no increase >1% in critical-field regressions vs. baseline.

Proposed evaluation plan (short):
1) Candidate models: run quick microbenchmarks on these variants: LlamaX-13B-int8, Redstone-7B-quant, and a tuned Amphora-12B (low-latency profile). We'll include generation/coverage and structured-output compliance.
2) Prompt & examples: use the attached prompt set (nova_prompt_set_v1.jsonl) with 300 labeled examples for round-1 and 2k for the full run.
3) Schema tests: automated JSON-schema validation, plus a focused fuzz suite for optional fields and nested arrays (see json_schema_spec_v2.json).
4) Fn-call/Tooling behavior: evaluate two failure modes — silent schema-misfill and tool-timeout. Recommendation: conservative retry policy (2 retries with exponential backoff 200ms->400ms) and a deterministic fallback model (smaller quantized variant) for timeouts.

Deliverables & timing:
- Microbench report (latency/cost/quality): 3 business days (we'll share the benchmark CSV).
- Full evaluation (2k sample run + schema regressions): 10 business days after kickoff.

Next steps / asks for you:
- Please confirm the 2k sample dataset can be shared (anonymized).
- Are there any columns that absolutely cannot be altered (PII or canonical IDs)? Call these out so we add strict regression checks.

Attachments: nova_fit_benchmarks_20290520.csv (empty stub for initial metrics), nova_prompt_set_v1.jsonl, json_schema_spec_v2.json

Thanks — I'll queue the microbenchmarks once you confirm data sharing.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

From: Alex Hart <alex.hart@novacare.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sethi <priya.sethi@novacare.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 17:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call follow-up: candidate models, JSON-schema QA & fn-call retry plan

Thanks Marcus — useful plan and clear asks. A few quick clarifications: 

- We can share an anonymized 2k sample (will remove patient names and SSNs). Expect to have that to you by EOD Wednesday.
- Critical fields: patient_id (canonical, must not be transformed), claim_id, and billing_code. Anything that changes these fails our acceptance.
- On retries: prefer the conservative approach, but can you add an observable flag in the response when a retry occurred so our ETL team can audit these records?

Also, can you include a short note on expected cost delta for running Amphora-12B vs the 7B quant variant for the 2k run? That will help us triage budget internally.

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Hart
Director, Data Platform — NovaCare
alex.hart@novacare.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 18:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call follow-up: candidate models, JSON-schema QA & fn-call retry plan

Looping in a couple of quick implementation notes for Marcus / Alex: 
- Visibility: we'll add a response field retry_info: {"attempts": n, "last_error": "timeout"} (we'll pass this as structured metadata in the output envelope so it doesn't interfere with schema fields).
- Cost estimate: rough ballpark for 2k-run (tokens ~1.2M) — Amphora-12B (tuned) ~= $1,800; Redstone-7B-quant ~= $650; LlamaX-13B-int8 ~= $1,100. I'll attach finer per-token breakdown in the microbench artifact.
- Schema enforcement: we'll run schema validation both pre-commit (at model output) and post-enrichment (after tool calls) to catch drift.

Will coordinate the microbench run once Marcus gets the sample.

— Neha
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Hart <alex.hart@novacare.com>, Priya Sethi <priya.sethi@novacare.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call follow-up: candidate models, JSON-schema QA & fn-call retry plan

Appreciate the fast replies — summary + quick action items: 

Action items (we own):
- Marcus: start microbenchmark suite as soon as anonymized 2k arrives (ETA: within 24 hours of receipt). Deliverable: nova_fit_benchmarks_20290520.csv + per-model cost/latency table.
- Neha: include retry_info envelope and add schema post-enrichment checks in the pipeline.
- Dylan: prepare the Amphora tuning run config and quantization test (will aim for latency target on 95th pct).

Action items (NovaCare):
- Alex / Priya: share anonymized 2k sample by EOD Wed (confirm required columns left intact for canonical IDs).
- Confirm whether the ETL team wants retries logged to a separate audit channel (we can post to a secure S3 or to a webhook).

Open concerns to highlight:
- Quality regression guardrails: we will set a hard stop if critical-field regression >1% during the full run. If that happens, we will (a) roll back to baseline, (b) produce a focused error analysis, and (c) propose mitigations (prompt engineering, higher-context windows, or custom fine-tune).
- Fn-call determinism: tool latency variance may still produce non-deterministic enrichment results; recommend adding a canonicalization step for enriched fields.

If this looks good, I’ll kick the microbench once we get the sample.

Thanks again — talk soon.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
